title: Dry, ferment and jar food products that sell

say: Dry, ferment and jar food products that sell.
This is the video for Module 4 of Advanced Cooking and Nutrition: food preservation and packaged products.
Preserving food lets you buy produce when it is cheap.

say: Microbes need water to grow, so removing water makes food keep for months. Step one. Sort, wash and slice evenly, about 6 to 8 mm thick, so pieces dry at the same speed.

panel.heading: From fresh produce to dried packs
items: Sort, wash and slice evenly, 6 to 8 mm
Blanch leafy greens; dip mango in lemon water
Dry in single layers in a covered solar dryer
Test: vegetables snap, fruit is leathery
Cool, pack airtight, label and date

say: Step two. Blanch leafy vegetables in boiling water for about 1 to 2 minutes, then cool them quickly. Dip mango in diluted lemon juice to limit browning.

panel.rule: Mould means discard the whole batch. Never pick it out.

say: In fermentation, friendly bacteria turn sugars into acid, which keeps harmful bacteria away. For ogi, steep clean maize for 1 to 3 days, changing the water daily.

panel.heading: Ogi and salt-brined vegetables
items: Ogi: steep 1 to 3 days, change water daily
Mill, sieve, then settle and sour
Brine: weigh salt at about 2% of vegetables
Keep vegetables under the brine
Vinegar pickles: 5% acidity, tested ratio

say: Mill it, sieve it with clean water, then let the starch settle and sour. Keep it cool and use within a few days.

say: For brined vegetables, weigh the salt. For example, Ruth in Jos used 2,000 g of cabbage and carrots, so 2,000 times 0.02 gives 40 g of salt. Spoons vary too much.

say: Fresh ogi and good ferments have a clean, pleasantly sour smell. A thin white film on brine is often a harmless yeast and can be skimmed.

panel.heading: When to throw a ferment away

say: But fuzzy mould of any colour, pink, grey or black patches, a slimy texture or a rotten smell mean the whole batch goes. Never taste a ferment that smells bad.

say: Write every formula as a percentage of the total weight, and any batch is just multiplication. Hadiza's suya spice is 55% kuli kuli powder, 20% dried chilli, 10% ginger, and 5% each of garlic, onion and salt.
For 5,000 g she needs 2,750 g of kuli kuli and 1,000 g of chilli. She checks the total adds back to 5,000 g.

say: Sauces with garlic, onion or pepper under oil can allow botulism to grow if not cooked and acidified properly. It is rare but can be fatal.
Keep opened jars in the fridge, and never claim months of shelf life at room temperature unless a food laboratory has tested it.

say: To remember. Dry in a covered dryer and cool before packing. Throw away any mouldy batch. Weigh your salt for ferments.
Write formulas in percentages and weigh every ingredient. Use sterilised jars and label sauces to refrigerate after opening.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Dry in a covered dryer; cool before packing
Mouldy batch? Discard it all
Weigh salt: about 2% for brined vegetables
Write formulas in percentages, weigh everything
Sterilised jars; refrigerate after opening
